call_points.text: Consolidated EBITDA margin should improve by at least 100 bps by FY27 end on operating leverage.
Marketing spend for the quarter was just under ₹5 Cr, largely IPL sponsorship.
LGD growers are talking of doubling their business over the next three years, driving certification volumes.
8-10 large LGD growers contribute close to 40-50% of revenues.
AGL will be extended globally, starting with a collection window and mobile laboratories in Jaipur.
The company remains debt-free; higher finance cost reflects rental payouts on additional office space.
Management declined to disclose carats graded by category, citing competitive reasons.
FY27 guided at 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth, with margins held at FY26 levels.
EBITDA growth above revenue comes from operating leverage; management sees no margin erosion.
Q4FY26 LGD certification revenue grew 35% and LGD jewelry 29%, on new customers and grower capacity additions.
Natural-diamond jewelry fell 19% in the quarter as high gold and silver prices slowed India demand.
LGD capacity additions are in Surat, and management says the full impact has not yet come through.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated the earlier point that Indian LGD growers keep adding capacity

call_points.text: Plan to expand AGL into markets beyond the US for colour stones.
Subsidiary business grew revenue 14% and EBITDA over 25% in the quarter, with margins up 100 bps.
Natural-diamond jewelry softness blamed on gold price volatility; management hopes it settles over the next quarter or two.
Global natural-diamond certification share estimated at 20-25%, with India above 50%.
Management says it is building a US sales organisation but declined to give headcount or a target size.
ASP is treated as a derivative of mix; management focuses on volume, revenue and EBITDA instead.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated the earlier point that realised price per report is a mix outcome

call_points.text: Certification stays on the traditional 4Cs format; retailers do not want a new nomenclature.
Total certification volumes for the 15M period stood at 16.45 Mn reports, reflecting a 20% YoY growth.
Group EBITDA for the 15M period stood at ₹972.8 Cr, implying a 22% YoY growth.
Group PAT for the 15M period stood at ₹711.2 Cr, registering a 25% YoY growth.
The company closed the 15M period with ₹800.5 Cr of cash and cash equivalents.
Certification revenues grew by 19% YoY, reaching ₹1,546.5 Cr during the 15M period.
Average realized price per report declined 1% YoY to ₹94 in the 15M period.
Indian LGD growers have increased capacity consistently over the years.

timeline.summary: International Gemmological Institute (India) Limited changed its name to International Gemological Institute Limited on May 04, 2026, per Manager Jeetendra Rangnani’s circular.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹368.56 Cr (+20.9% YoY), net profit ₹179.6 Cr (+27.6% YoY).
International Gemological Institute reported 15M FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,597.6 Cr and PAT of ₹711.2 Cr.
International Gemological Institute Limited hosted an earnings call on May 20, 2026, for Q4FY26 and FY26 results, with recording available at investor.igi.org.
On its 20 May 2026 Q4 and 15-month FY26 earnings call, International Gemological Institute guided FY27 revenue growth at 15% and EBITDA growth at 20%, with margins held at FY26 levels.
Q1FY27 earnings call: revenue ₹370.8 Cr (+23% YoY), EBITDA ₹223.8 Cr (+29%), PAT ₹165.7 Cr (+31%); FY27 guidance held at 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA growth.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹398.02 Cr (+31.0% YoY), net profit ₹185.84 Cr (+43.2% YoY).
International Gemological Institute Limited reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹398.02 Cr (+31% YoY) and net profit of ₹185.84 Cr (+43% YoY).
International Gemological Institute Limited shared its earnings call audio for Q2 & H1 FY27 on October 21, 2026, available at investor.igi.org.
International Gemological Institute reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹398.02 Cr (+31% YoY) and net profit of ₹185.84 Cr (+43% YoY), upgrading its full-year outlook.
